correctness.rationale: For each feasible chain the convex spectral norm admits dihedral symmetrization without relaxing any individual rim floor. All nontrivial wheel eigenvalues split into one radial and m-1 Fourier modes, leaving a 2-variable minimax. Explicit V-shaped rim minimization, a uniform lower bound suppressing the negative radial branch, and three algebraic switch conditions prove the closed four-piece formula, optimal invariant probabilities and all endpoints for every m>=4. Independent finite LP enumeration checked 1,833 numerical cases, including transition points, and 48 exact-rational cases; tests are supplementary rather than proof. The proof does not assert universal uniqueness of nonsymmetric optima.

evidence: The known unconstrained optimum has p=1/m and q=tau_1, giving exactly the first branch. Enforcing q>=tau>tau_1 rules it out.

The new remaining branches have q=tau, p=1-(a+b)tau/2, then p=(2-b tau)/(m+2), then p=1-2tau. These are independent constrained optima whose exact thresholds do not follow from an unconstrained minimizing point alone.
For odd m, b<4 creates a nontrivial final zero-holding regime; even m has b=4 and the final regime collapses to the endpoint.

value.rationale: A lower bound on each rim transition encodes a natural local-exploration requirement in a hub-mediated network. The complete formula quantifies the cost of that constraint for every wheel size and every feasible floor, including three exact phase boundaries and a parity-sensitive final zero-holding phase. It supplies globally optimal feasible kernels, not only a computational solution or small-graph numerical increment; it does not claim a new graph spectrum or general SDP formulation.
